articles.title: Week 9: Mossdeep returns, Saffron counts the cost, Lavender gets another test
articles.dek: Tessa Wren calls all fifteen games, including Petalburg at Cinnabar, and asks whether Sunyshore can keep running without Myles Gabite.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Mara won Week 8 at 11–3. I went 10–4, Dorian finished 8–6, Rowan 7–7 and Ellis 6–8. Rowan did call Fortree's first victory, a result the rest of us would rather discuss after he has left the room. Closest-score bonuses went five apiece to Rowan, Mara and Ellis, two to me and one to Dorian. They remain a separate competition; a beautifully measured losing pick is still a losing pick.

My Eterna keys held up: keep Olivine below one hundred rushing yards and score before halftime. The Thorns allowed 44 on the ground and had two first-half touchdowns. Sunyshore was a less tidy success. I asked for sixty percent passing and no more than two sacks; DeZhaun Watzon went ten of eighteen with one sack. The Starseekers won behind 221 rushing yards. I picked the winner while assigning too much of the repair to the passing game.

Now Mossdeep returns from its bye at 7–0, Saffron must replace two injured linebackers, and Sunyshore visits Lavender without Myles Gabite. Mt. Silver and Snowpoint rest. The Reds can enjoy 8–0 without another forecast from me; the other thirty clubs get fifteen games, seventy-five panel picks and at least one disagreement worth keeping until next week. Petalburg at Cinnabar is my closest contender matchup. Fortree at Fuchsia is my test of whether a first win can become a useful habit.

matchups.matchup: Dewford's missing runners against Viridian's stalled offense
matchups.analysis: Both teams are 4–4, but Brawly has the more immediate personnel problem. Unfezant ran for 89 yards against Pewter and is now out for two weeks; Excadrill also remains unavailable. Frosmoth threw two touchdowns and two interceptions in that win. Viridian was shut out by Rustboro, yet Gabite still gained ninety yards on 21 carries. I narrowly prefer the Titans to get a steadier sequence of possessions from their remaining ground game. Dewford needs its receivers to carry more of the load than last week's twelve completions allowed.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least fifteen passes and throw no interceptions.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for one hundred yards and finish two touchdown drives.

matchups.matchup: Dragapult's passing volume against Pewter's scoring shortage
matchups.analysis: Pewter has scored 64 points in eight games and lost three straight. Mauville's 98 points are hardly a sales brochure, but Dragapult's 172 passing yards at Cinnabar suggest more ways to advance than the Rockers have consistently found. Two interceptions ruined that afternoon. Wyrdeer was more accurate for Pewter, completing sixteen of twenty-two, and Heatmor caught seven. Brock can make this uncomfortable by repeating that patient distribution. I still lean toward the Dynamos to find an extra touchdown against a secondary missing Scolipede and Venusaur.
matchups.awayKey: Give away the ball no more than once and score two touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least half of third downs and allow no completion over thirty yards.

matchups.matchup: My Way, Son makes Celadon defend the next handoff
matchups.analysis: Rustboro's 223 rushing yards at Viridian included 151 from My Way, Son. That is the most persuasive unit in this matchup, even with Porygon-Z throwing for only 58. Celadon has become harder to dismiss: its last three opponents scored ten, nine and thirteen. Delibird supplied 104 receiving yards in the latest win, including a third-and-fourteen touchdown. Erika can keep this close if that passing threat makes Rustboro chase. I prefer the Stone because their ground game offers repeated progress without needing another exceptional conversion.
matchups.awayKey: Run for at least 150 yards and avoid losing a fumble.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Rustboro below five yards per carry and complete two touchdown passes.

matchups.matchup: Petalburg's rested offense against the Blaze's third-down resistance
matchups.analysis: The Pride return at 5–2 after a bye; Cinnabar is 6–2 and has allowed ten points or fewer in three straight wins. Petalburg's last game was a 17–14 loss at Mt. Silver, where a late touchdown arrived without a final chance to complete the comeback. Norman needs earlier scoring against another defense comfortable keeping the game small. Cinnabar intercepted Dragapult twice and sacked him three times last week. The Blaze also finished their last possession with a fourteen-yard completion on third-and-nine. I like that combination of pressure and an offensive answer when the clock becomes part of the contest. Petalburg's defense, allowing 71 rushing yards a game, can force Blaine to win through Gholdengo. I expect him to do it, narrowly.
matchups.awayKey: Allow at most two sacks and score a touchdown in each half.
matchups.homeKey: Keep Petalburg below twenty points and convert five third downs.

matchups.matchup: Cerulean's contested catches meet Mossdeep's two ways to score
matchups.analysis: Both clubs rested after Week 7, when Cerulean beat Sunyshore 12–6 and Mossdeep beat Lavender 63–10. Misty's defense broke up nine passes in its win, including three consecutive attempts on the Starseekers' last possession. That is a credible argument for slowing Dram Marino. It is a less complete answer to an Eclipse offense with 1,131 rushing yards alongside 1,782 through the air. Accel BeckhmJr scored five receiving touchdowns in Mossdeep's last game; asking Cerulean to erase every threat is asking too much. The Tide have scored 96 points in seven games. Four field goals would leave them needing an extraordinary defensive afternoon against Michael Dorrill's club. I expect Cerulean to produce some stops and still run short of points.
matchups.awayKey: Reach 140 rushing yards and allow no more than two sacks.
matchups.homeKey: Finish three touchdown drives and hold Mossdeep below thirty points.

matchups.matchup: A changed Saffron defense and an unchanged receiving problem for opponents
matchups.analysis: Verrick Brooks and Ninetales are each out for four weeks. Trent Scarboro cannot replace those absences by pointing at Saffron's 43 points allowed all season. Sootopolis has its own loss: Heatmor is out for six weeks after catching five passes at Violet. The Surge managed nine points there, while Archam Manning threw for 350 and Gengar Pickens caught two touchdowns against Pastoria. I expect Saffron's offense to give its altered defense enough room. The Corps should remember that the 44–9 final began with a nine-point deficit.
matchups.awayKey: Sustain three scoring drives and surrender no return touchdown.
matchups.homeKey: Complete two touchdown passes and hold the Surge below eighty rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: Drakloak's opportunities against Lavaridge's recovery week
matchups.analysis: Vermilion's 5–2 record now comes with a one-point season scoring margin after Fortree's 34–10 win. Exploud, the runner wearing 87, is out for twelve weeks; the Volts already had another Exploud sidelined. Lavaridge returns from a bye after losing 42–0 at Blackthorn. Neither team should assume the other will politely supply confidence. Drakloak's two catches for 88 yards last week still give Lt. Surge a reason to attack downfield, though nine targets produced those two receptions. I favor Vermilion with very little enthusiasm for a comfortable margin.
matchups.awayKey: Score before halftime and avoid conceding a passing play of forty yards.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least eighteen passes and lose no fumbles.

matchups.matchup: Rabsca tries to make the first win repeatable
matchups.analysis: Fortree's first victory came with 262 passing yards, three touchdown throws and no interceptions from Rabsca. Basculegion caught two of the scores. Fuchsia has now lost cornerback Kleavor for ten weeks, making that connection an immediate concern for Koga. Fortree also lost Mothim, Pawmot and Ampharos for two weeks apiece, so last week's lineup cannot simply be carried forward intact. Empoleon completed sixteen of twenty-three against Celadon. I expect enough passing on both sides to keep this lively, with the Skyhawks finding the better finishing opportunities.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and score three offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Keep Basculegion out of the end zone and win the turnover margin.

matchups.matchup: Gabite's yardage against a Swarm offense learning to stay on the field
matchups.analysis: Azalea has won four straight. Drampa completed 23 passes against Cianwood, nine to Hippopotas, while the Swarm converted eight of twelve third downs. Canalave can challenge that control with Gabite, who ran for 131 yards against Hearthome. Two lost fumbles and a missed late field goal turned the production into a 14–13 defeat. I prefer Bugsy's team at home because its passing game currently supplies more dependable continuation. Canalave's route to an answer is visible in those 168 team rushing yards, if it can keep them attached to possession.
matchups.awayKey: Lose no fumbles and produce two rushing touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Convert six third downs and limit Gabite to fewer than one hundred rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: Two passing attacks trying to stop helping the defense
matchups.analysis: Olivine was shut out at Eterna. Oreburgh lost at Veilstone after three interceptions. That is sufficient material for two blunt quarterback meetings. Farigiraf's injury absence has cleared for the Miners, but the next assignment is a choice for Roark; Cryogonal threw the three picks. Jasmine's club allowed only 24 rushing yards last week and generated three sacks. I lean toward that defensive work producing another modest score, this time with enough offense to win. Gabite needs more room than his 35 rushing yards in Eterna provided.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and score two offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for eighty yards and prevent a touchdown before halftime.

matchups.matchup: Cianwood's quarterback shortage against Eterna's repeated stops
matchups.analysis: Wigglytuff completed four of sixteen passes for 33 yards in Azalea. Gardevoir remains out for nine weeks. Eterna just held Olivine to 183 total yards and has allowed 58 points in seven games. The Thorns' own offense is uneven, but Slowking found Cramorant eight times for 119 yards in the shutout. That gives Gardenia a convincing way to turn defensive stops into an advantage. I expect the Crushers to struggle to keep pace even if their defense makes Eterna work for every possession.
matchups.awayKey: Hold Cianwood below 150 passing yards and commit no turnovers.
matchups.homeKey: Convert five third downs and score a first-half touchdown.

matchups.matchup: Gurdurr's volume against Pastoria's thin running game
matchups.analysis: Iron Jugulis threw 51 times in Violet's 13–9 win, with Gurdurr catching thirteen passes for 113 yards. That is plenty of movement for a small score. Pastoria led Saffron 9–0 before conceding 44 unanswered points, and its sixteen carries produced only 24 yards. Oinkologne is still out for six weeks. I expect Falkner's offense to manufacture more chances than the Waves, although another thirteen-point afternoon would invite trouble. Kilowattrel's 53-yard touchdown last week is a reminder that Pastoria can change the score without a long drive.
matchups.awayKey: Gain eighty rushing yards and allow no more than one passing touchdown.
matchups.homeKey: Turn three possessions into scores and avoid an interception.

matchups.matchup: Scol Alexander against Lavender's chance to keep a lead
matchups.analysis: Lavender led Blackthorn 17–6 before allowing three unanswered touchdowns. The defeat was much closer than the previous week's rout, and Hobbes ran for 89 yards on ten carries. Sunyshore supplied its own ground-game argument: Scol Alexander gained 165 of the team's 221 rushing yards against Mahogany. Myles Gabite is now out for five weeks and Fred Whirler for one, leaving Karson Jones less room to spread the workload. Watzon threw two interceptions in the win. Travis Scarboro's club can punish a repeat if Mr. Clanky builds on fifteen completions in twenty-two attempts. I still favor the Starseekers because their defense held Mahogany to 22 rushing yards, and Alexander offers a way to advance without demanding that every Watzon possession become a passing demonstration.
matchups.awayKey: Avoid turnovers in the second half and rush for 150 yards.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no reception longer than thirty yards and score in the fourth quarter.

matchups.matchup: Palafin's second assignment against Mahogany's effort to recover the run
matchups.analysis: Palafin scored on a run and a reception in Hearthome's 14–13 win at Canalave. With Luxray still out for seven weeks, those touches matter beyond one afternoon. Mahogany forced three turnovers in Sunyshore and lost because its offense produced only 168 yards, including 22 rushing. Dugtrio remains unavailable for one week. I narrowly favor the Frost at home: their defense created chances against a stronger running performance than Hearthome has shown. Fantina's team can change my mind by extending drives without relying on another pair of opposing fumbles.
matchups.awayKey: Convert six third downs and allow no more than one sack.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for ninety yards and hold Palafin below five yards per carry.

matchups.matchup: Hatterene's accuracy against a defense fresh from three interceptions
matchups.analysis: Blackthorn has won five straight, and Hatterene completed 27 of 29 passes against Lavender. Exploud caught all eight targets; Grovyle caught all seven. Veilstone intercepted Oreburgh three times but produced only 181 yards and converted one of eleven third downs. Maylene needs those takeaways against a much more accurate passer, or an offensive improvement large enough to make them unnecessary. I expect Clair's receivers to keep supplying the easier answer. The Fists are 4–0 at home and 0–4 away; this trip offers little immediate relief.
matchups.awayKey: Take the ball away twice and sustain two touchdown drives.
matchups.homeKey: Complete seventy percent of passes and avoid losing a fumble.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Unfezant's absence hurts, but Swellow caught a touchdown and gives Frosmoth somewhere useful to look. Viridian just managed 79 passing yards. I'm backing Dewford to find the less congested route to fifteen points.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Rustboro pushed Viridian around on the ground. Dewford would normally attack that weakness, but losing Unfezant and still missing Excadrill changes the assignment. I expect Gabite's available carries to decide this one for Giovanni.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: A shutout can make a team seem further from competence than it is. Gabite's ninety yards gave Viridian something to retain; Dewford is trying to replace its leading runner. That difference earns the Titans my cautious vote.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Viridian scored ZERO against Rustboro. Now we're offering the Titans another win on credit because Dewford has injuries? Frosmoth threw two touchdown passes last week. Give me those receivers and a Breakers road win.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Titans still have a runner who produced ninety yards during a dreadful offensive afternoon. Dewford's remaining backs face a larger adjustment, so I expect Viridian to sustain the more reliable scoring possessions.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pewter's eight points per game is an argument with a very small vocabulary. Dragapult can make mistakes and still offer more scoring possibilities. Mauville wins a game that probably will not require an overflow highlights package.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Heatmor's seven receptions give Pewter a workable answer underneath. I still expect Mauville's greater passing production to force the Rockers beyond that comfortable pace. Dragapult has enough targets to make Brock defend more ground.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Wyrdeer completed sixteen of twenty-two without an interception last week. In a game likely to punish impatience, I can see that steadiness outlasting Dragapult's riskier afternoon. Pewter gets a small win, and no grand rehabilitation speech.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Brock's team has managed 64 points in eight games. Sixty-four. Mauville doesn't have to become a powerhouse to beat that; Dragapult simply needs to stop supplying opposing defenders. I'm taking the Dynamos and the larger offensive ceiling.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mauville's passing volume should create one more useful opportunity against Pewter's depleted coverage. The Rockers can shorten the contest through Heatmor, but I don't expect their recent scoring level to support a full comeback.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: My Way, Son ran for 151 yards, and Celadon has spent three weeks keeping scores small rather than making opponents disappear. Rustboro can win this with ordinary handoffs. The Stone finally have a plan that doesn't require artistic finishing.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Erika's defense has allowed ten, nine and thirteen in its last three games. Make Rustboro finish through the air and those 58 passing yards start to matter. Delibird gives Celadon the bigger passing-play threat; I'm taking the Bloom.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Rustboro's last loss contained plenty of useful rushing work, and the shutout preserved it while fixing the result. I expect Tyler Scarboro to keep trusting My Way, Son. Celadon will make them earn the lead without erasing it.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Two hundred twenty-three rushing yards. That's Rustboro's application, and I'm approving it. Celadon's recent resistance is admirable, but an offense with 75 points all season cannot keep asking its defense to negotiate every inch alone.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Celadon should defend more stubbornly than Viridian did. I still favor Rustboro's ability to collect repeated rushing gains, because the Bloom's passing improvement has yet to produce enough points to make that approach uncomfortable.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cinnabar has conceded nineteen points in three straight wins. Petalburg's rest is useful; it is not a touchdown. I expect another small Blaze victory, with everyone discovering Gholdengo's final third-down completion just as the exits open.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Petalburg made Mt. Silver defend a genuine late comeback. Give Norman a rested offense and I expect earlier pressure this time. The Pride's run defense can leave Cinnabar leaning on passing downs; I'm taking Petalburg to win those exchanges.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Pride's last defeat ended without another possession after their touchdown. I trust them to create more chances before the urgent part this time. Cinnabar deserves respect, but Petalburg has enough balance to leave with a narrow win.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Blaine has allowed ten points or fewer in three consecutive victories, yet somehow Cinnabar is still being introduced as a pleasant surprise. Petalburg is good. The Blaze are better at making opponents play their game. Cinnabar wins again.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Gholdengo's third-and-nine completion helped close out Mauville. I expect Cinnabar's pressure to keep this close enough for that kind of offensive decision to matter again, and I narrowly prefer the home team's closing answer.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cerulean can collect pass breakups while Mossdeep collects points through the run. The Eclipse have 307 in seven games and two productive routes to them. I like the Tide's defense; I don't like its assignment nearly enough to pick it.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Misty made Sunyshore's last four throws fail. Michael Dorrill can answer that resistance with a running game that has already gained 1,131 yards. Mossdeep doesn't need Dram Marino to force every possession through contested catches. Eclipse, comfortably.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Tide earned their win over Sunyshore, and I won't reduce it to four fortunate kicks. Mossdeep still asks more questions of a defense than Cerulean's offense is likely to answer. Seven wins should become eight.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I remain entirely capable of questioning Mossdeep's coronation while recognizing that Cerulean has scored 96 points in seven games. The Tide need touchdowns against this offense. I do not expect them to find enough. The Eclipse win this one.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Cerulean's coverage can interrupt individual throws, but Mossdeep can keep advancing through Ninjaskamara and the rest of its rushing game. I expect the Eclipse to create too many sustained scoring chances for the Tide's modest offense.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Saffron loses two linebackers and still brings Archam Manning, Gengar Pickens and a six-game winning streak. Sootopolis just lost Heatmor after scoring nine. The injury report has changed; my belief in a Psi Corps victory has not.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Wallace needs sustained offense to test Saffron's replacements. A running game that gained only 22 yards at Violet leaves too much to a passing attack now missing Heatmor. I expect the Corps to control the useful downs.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Brooks and Ninetales will be missed, but Saffron's offense supplied 453 yards last week. That gives the new defensive combination some room to settle. Sootopolis has a harder time replacing the catches it just lost with Heatmor.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Forty-four unanswered points is an emphatic way to correct a slow start. Trent Scarboro has offensive weapons that Sootopolis hasn't shown it can match. The linebackers' absences make the assignment harder; they don't make the Surge my pick.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Pickens' 176 receiving yards show why Saffron can absorb a less dominant defensive afternoon. Sootopolis needs more sustained production than its recent running game has offered, and I expect the Corps to score often enough to protect their lead.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Vermilion is 5–2 and has outscored opponents by ONE point. Add another injured Exploud and I am taking Lavaridge's rested chance to make the record look less impressive. The Inferno win an ugly one by a point.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavaridge allowed Hatterene to complete thirty of thirty-five passes before the bye. Drakloak needs fewer catches than that to hurt a defense. I expect Vermilion to attack those opportunities while its damaged running game finds smaller supporting work.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: I understand the temptation to discard Vermilion after Fortree. Drakloak still gained 88 yards on two catches, and Lavaridge's last defensive performance offers another opening. I'll take a limited Volts recovery without pretending the injuries have vanished.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Vermilion's record is doing an enormous amount of public-relations work for its offense. The backfield keeps losing players, and Fortree just exposed the coverage. I expect Lavaridge to return from its bye with enough passing success to win.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Volts' injuries make a comfortable rebound difficult to expect. Drakloak nevertheless gives Chandelure a scoring threat against a defense coming off a 42-point concession, which is enough for my narrow Vermilion pick.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Rabsca threw three touchdowns without an interception, and Fuchsia has just lost Kleavor. That's a fairly direct invitation to try again. Fortree's own injuries will trim the celebration, but Basculegion can keep the useful part going.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Basculegion caught two touchdowns against Vermilion. Koga now has to defend that connection without Kleavor, and Fuchsia allowed Celadon a touchdown on third-and-fourteen. I expect Fortree's passing game to provide the decisive finish again.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Fortree deserves its first celebration. It also has three new absences, including Mothim, before visiting a team whose quarterback completed sixteen of twenty-three last week. I'm giving Empoleon a narrow home escape while the Skyhawks adjust.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: One Fortree win has apparently settled the entire future. I disagree. Mothim, Pawmot and Ampharos are out, and Empoleon has been completing passes even in defeat. I'm calling Fuchsia to punish those missing pieces and win decisively.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Fuchsia's loss of Kleavor opens a difficult coverage assignment just as Rabsca and Basculegion arrive with a productive game behind them. I expect Fortree to finish more passing possessions, even with its own injured contributors unavailable.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Four straight wins are a useful answer to the question of whether Azalea has improved. Drampa completed 23 passes; Canalave threw for 95 yards. I prefer the offense with more ways to keep the next possession alive.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Canalave can run, but two fumbles turned a productive day into another rescue attempt. Azalea converted eight of twelve third downs. I expect Bugsy's passing game to keep Gabite waiting long enough for the Swarm to take control.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Gabite's 131 yards should keep Canalave involved. Azalea's recent progress feels broader, with Hippopotas giving Drampa a reliable receiving outlet. I favor the Swarm to make the steadier decisions in another close fourth quarter.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Canalave ran for 168 yards and handed the result away with two fumbles. Azalea has allowed 1,001 rushing yards this season. Keep the ball, feed Gabite, and stop asking this matchup to be complicated. I'm calling a Bulwark statement.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Swarm's passing game is extending drives through repeated catches rather than one isolated explosion. I expect that consistency to outlast Canalave's rushing threat, though another strong Gabite performance would keep the margin narrow.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Oreburgh's three interceptions were dreadful, but its defense allowed only 181 yards and collected three sacks. Olivine just scored zero. I'm backing the Miners to turn a little offensive restraint into a road win the Ironclads cannot chase.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Jasmine's defense held Eterna to 24 rushing yards and sacked Slowking three times. That gives Olivine a concrete route against another uncertain passing attack. I expect the Ironclads to win the difficult downs and a very small game.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Being shut out makes every offensive flaw feel permanent. Olivine still has Gabite and a defense that pressured Slowking. Oreburgh's quarterback decision adds another uncertainty, so I'll take the hosts to recover enough of their ordinary work.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Oreburgh forced eight Veilstone punts and still lost because it threw the ball to three defenders. Those defensive stops deserve an offense that gives them a chance. I'm picking a Miners correction against an Olivine team that just went scoreless.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Olivine generated pressure and restrained the run even during its shutout loss. I expect that defensive combination to make Oreburgh's next quarterback afternoon difficult, while the Ironclads find just enough scoring to separate themselves.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Four completions for 33 yards is a dangerous starting point against Eterna. The Thorns have allowed 58 points all season. I expect Cramorant to do enough receiving work that nobody has to describe twenty points as an offensive avalanche.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Eterna made Olivine punt five times and held its running game to 44 yards. Cianwood's current passing attack offers even less relief when the ground game stalls. Gardenia should get repeated opportunities to put the Crushers behind.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Cianwood is asking Wigglytuff to carry an injured offense, and Eterna is a particularly unkind opponent for that lesson. Slowking's connection with Cramorant gives the Thorns enough progress to let their defense keep setting the terms.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Eterna has conceded 58 points in seven games. Cianwood completed four passes last week. I am willing to make controversial predictions; I am not required to ignore the entire available afternoon. The Thorns win with their defense.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Crushers are struggling to keep drives alive without Gardevoir. Eterna's defense should shorten those possessions, and Cramorant's eight-catch performance gives Slowking a practical way to turn the resulting chances into points.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Violet threw 51 passes to score thirteen points. That's a lot of paperwork, but Gurdurr's thirteen catches show there was progress underneath it. Pastoria's running game offers less stability, so the Falcons get my vote and another editing assignment.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Pastoria's Kilowattrel produced a 53-yard touchdown against Saffron. Violet needed 51 throws to reach thirteen points. I expect the Waves to create the more valuable completions and make that inefficient passing volume costly for Falkner.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Waves' nine-point lead at Saffron deserves a little memory, even after the collapse. Violet has a more repeatable receiving outlet in Gurdurr, though. I expect those shorter gains to keep the Falcons from needing a dramatic finish.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Fifty-one passes. Thirteen points. Violet has turned passing volume into an endurance event. Kilowattrel can change a game on one catch, and I expect Pastoria's defense to make the Falcons regret asking for another long examination.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Gurdurr gives Iron Jugulis a target who can repeatedly extend a possession. Pastoria's missing Oinkologne leaves less support for its own passing game, so I expect Violet to accumulate more chances and finally convert enough of them.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Sunyshore threw two interceptions and lost a fumble while escaping Mahogany. Now Myles Gabite is out and Lavender has a quarterback coming off fifteen completions in twenty-two attempts. I'm taking the Wails to turn improved play into an actual win.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavender let a 17–6 lead disappear because Blackthorn kept finding productive throws. Sunyshore can threaten a different weakness through Scol Alexander's running. I expect Karson Jones to lean on those gains and demand fewer risky answers from Watzon.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Lavender's first half at Blackthorn looked like a team recovering its footing. Mr. Clanky was more accurate, and Hobbes kept moving. With Sunyshore losing Myles Gabite and still throwing costly interceptions, I can see Travis Scarboro finishing this one differently.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Sunyshore gained 318 yards and still needed its defense to survive three giveaways. Lavender has endured enough passing punishment to recognize an opening when Watzon provides one. I'm calling Mr. Clanky and the Wails to make the home chance count.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Alexander's 165 rushing yards give Sunyshore a credible way to reduce the burden on Watzon. I expect the Starseekers' run defense to limit Hobbes enough that Lavender has to keep answering through the air, where its last comeback stalled.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Hearthome found a useful answer in Palafin, who scored twice after Luxray went out. Mahogany's twenty rushing attempts gained 22 yards. I'll take the Haunts to keep the Frost's offense uncomfortable and escape with something less delicate than one point.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Mahogany created three turnovers against Sunyshore. Hearthome won despite gaining only 189 yards, and I expect Pryce's defense to make those short possessions expensive. The Frost can win without asking their damaged running game for a spectacular day.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Frost lost after giving themselves several defensive chances. Dugtrio is still absent, but I trust Mahogany to recover more ordinary offensive progress at home. Hearthome's close win deserves credit without becoming a promise of another one.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Hearthome won by one while allowing 168 rushing yards. Mahogany's ground game was miserable in Sunyshore, but this is a much more forgiving assignment. Pryce gets enough production back to make the defensive takeaways matter this time.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Palafin gives Hearthome a workable replacement, but Mahogany's defense has just shown it can create extra possessions. I expect the Frost to turn one of those chances into the separation that their offense failed to provide last week.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Hatterene missed twice in 29 attempts. Veilstone's latest win required three interceptions and came with one conversion in eleven third downs. I expect Blackthorn to remove the free gifts and leave the Fists with the longer afternoon.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Grovyle caught all seven targets and Exploud all eight against Lavender. That reliable distribution should make Veilstone earn its stops without waiting for Cryogonal's mistakes to repeat. Clair has the more sustainable passing attack by a large margin.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Veilstone has done all its winning at home, and this trip asks its offense to keep up with Hatterene's accuracy. I would like a reason to make Blackthorn's afternoon awkward. The recent receiving work doesn't provide one.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Blackthorn completed 27 passes in 29 attempts. Veilstone converted ONE third down in eleven. Maylene needs takeaways to bridge that difference, and Hatterene is being exceptionally uncooperative. The Dragons keep their winning streak moving.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The Fists' defense won its last game with interceptions, but Blackthorn's accurate passing offers fewer such invitations. I expect the Dragons to build sustained drives while Veilstone's offense struggles to stay on the field long enough to answer.

editions.pickRecordMethod: Straight-up winner, actual ties separately. Closest score uses abs(predicted away - actual away) + abs(predicted home - actual home). Every panelist tied for lowest error gets one shared closest bonus; bonuses are independent of correct winner and do not alter the W-L record.
